decisionRules: Admit bounded portable run coordinates, credential-safe request material, typed operations, execution limits, and an acyclic dependency graph before consulting snapshot, checkpoint, lease, or mutation collaborators.
Bind one run ID to one plan digest, expected remote revision, lease generation, and durable batch checkpoint.

Read the remote after execution and accept the run when its revision and state digest match the durable reconciled checkpoint.

failureModes: The operation graph can carry unresolved dependencies, a cycle, a field outside the typed contract, or an operation larger than the request envelope.
A service-issued identifier can expand a previously admitted batch beyond its request envelope.
Another writer can retain the lease or the remote revision can move after planning.
A request can receive a bounded retry signal, time out before application, or lose a success response after application.
Execution can stop after remote acceptance and before the next durable checkpoint.
A writer can lose its lease while a remote or checkpoint call is in flight, and a successor generation can take authority.
Remote revision or state can drift after an interrupted application or after the final durable checkpoint.
A remote response can omit, repeat, misidentify, or reshape operation results.
A remote can contain a partial intent set that needs an accountable reconciliation decision.
recoveryMoves: Return the exact operation, dependency, field, or byte boundary to the plan owner before remote work begins.
Remeasure the fully resolved batch before dispatch and return its exact replanning coordinate when issued identifiers expand the representation.
Wait for lease expiry or return the observed revision and form a current plan from remote truth.
Honor the bounded delay or read intent results and classify the batch before replay.
Resume the same plan and stable intent IDs from the earlier checkpoint; idempotent remote results advance the run.
Fence each checkpoint write with the current lease generation, renew around the awaited store call, and reconcile remote intent results when a successor generation takes authority.
Compare the observed revision and state digest with the durable expected coordinates and route drift to batch or final reconciliation.

Admit every remote snapshot and one exact result for each requested operation before hashing, classification, or checkpoint advancement, and return typed protocol friction when either response contract differs.
Return applied and absent intent identities to a human decision owner while preserving both coordinates.
